action_items: None — BUG-445 fix is verified shippable. bucketInHouse correctly classifies checkout===business_date as 'leaving' and checkout<business_date as 'stayover' (retaining the red OVERDUE Nd pill). Counts, chips and tile all reconcile with backend counts.leaving_today/in_house/arrived_today.
critical_code_review_comments: frontDeskTransform.js L84-90 — bucketInHouse is now a clean 3-way classifier keyed off ISO string compare vs meta.business_date (no browser clock). The BUG-445 marker on L87 correctly reads `row.checkout === bd` before the arrived branch — an overdue guest (checkout < bd) short-circuits neither branch and correctly falls through to 'stayover'. Pure and unit-testable.

InHousePanel.jsx uses useChipCounts(rows, bucketInHouse, bd, CHIP_ORDER.inhouse) and filters visible rows via `bucketInHouse(r, bd) === chip` — same predicate for counts and rows, so chip counter is guaranteed consistent with rendered rows. Good invariant.

KpiTabStrip.jsx tile 'In-House' sub-lines read counts.arrived_today and counts.leaving_today directly (server counts, AC-12) — the chip contract is derived client-side but happens to reconcile to the server counts under the current rule. If the server ever changes leaving_today semantics, the two could drift; consider adding a runtime dev-only assertion (dev build only) that chipCounts.leaving === counts.leaving_today when rows are loaded.

Status pill text is 'Overdue 1 d' in the DOM but 'OVERDUE 1 D' visually via CSS text-transform. Automated tests that grep the raw text should use case-insensitive matching or read the computed style — a minor authoring hazard for future test agents (spec used 'OVERDUE N d').
